8 ارتثأ It (milk) thickened, or became thick: (S, K:) and so ↓ ارثأ , (M, K,) in some one or more of the dialects. (M.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] ارتثأ عَلَيْهِمْ أَمْرُهُمْ (assumed tropical:) Their case, or affair, became confused to them. (S, M.) And ارتثأ فِى رَأْيِهِ (assumed tropical:) He made a confusion in his judgment, or opinion. (S, K.) And هُمْ يَرْتَثِئُونَ أَمْرَهُمْ (assumed tropical:) [app. for فِى أَمْرِهِمْ, and thus meaning They are confused, or they make a confusion, in their case, or affair: or, otherwise, they confuse their case, or affair]: from الرَّثِيْئَة; (T, TA;) and if so, tropical. (TA.) ＝
-A2- Also He drank what is termed رَثِيْئَة. (T, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
